title.narrative: ASEAN-Korea Cooperation for Methane Mitigation - Brunei & Malaysia

description.narrative: The ASEAN-Korea Cooperation on Methane Mitigation (AKCMM) project, implemented by GGGI and funded through the ASEAN-Korea Cooperation Fund (AKCF) with a budget of USD 20M, supports Malaysia and Brunei in advancing their national methane mitigation agendas. For the two countries, the project is structured around three core outputs: Output 1 focuses on developing enabling policies and institutions for methane governance; Output 2 aims to improve the measurement of methane emissions through upgraded inventory methodologies and enhanced MMRV systems; and Output 4 promotes regional dialogue and partnership among ASEAN Member States and the Republic of Korea (ROK). In Malaysia, implementation is anchored through the Methane Reduction Committee (MRC), formally endorsed through the National Steering Committee on Climate Change (NSCCC) under the Ministry of Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability (NRES). In Brunei, engagement is being pursued through continuous institutional consultations, specifically with the Brunei Climate Change Office (BCCO). The project utilizes a consulting consortium that includes Seoul National University and technical firm Weatherpia, drawing upon their international expertise to deliver gap analysis reports, capacity-building programs, and methane reduction planning support tailored to each country's national context and policy priorities.

The overarching objective of the AKCMM project is to strengthen institutional, technical, and policy capacities in Malaysia and Brunei to effectively measure, report, and reduce methane emissions in line with their respective Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) and GMP commitments (for Malaysia). The project seeks to establish robust governance structures for methane mitigation, improve the accuracy and transparency of national methane inventories through upgraded MRV and MMRV (measuring, monitoring, reporting, and verification) frameworks, and catalyze the development of actionable National MRPs. In doing so, the project contributes to broader regional climate ambitions under ASEAN, supports alignment with the 1.5°C pathway, and positions both countries to leverage international financial and technical resources for low-carbon transition. An important secondary objective is to foster South–South and triangular cooperation, with the ROK serving as a knowledge partner offering benchmarked approaches in methane management that can be adapted to the ASEAN context.
